data.gender_notes: Damanraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Damanraj is a Sanskrit name, derived from the words 'daman' (control) and 'raj' (king). The name symbolizes the power of controlling one's own mind and ruling over it, which is considered a great virtue in Hinduism. The name Damanraj carries the meaning “Controller of the mind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Damanraj usually hope their child will grow to embody controller of the mind and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Damanraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Controller of the mind.”

data.cultural_impact: The name "Damanraj" highlights the importance of self-discipline and control in Hindu culture. It represents the idea of mastering one's emotions and desires and ruling over them, rather than being ruled by them. This idea is reflected in various aspects of Hindu life, from religious practices to everyday behavior. For example, the practice of yoga and meditation is meant to help individuals gain control over their minds and bodies.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Damanraj" has deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It reflects the importance of inner peace and mental control in spiritual growth. In Hindu philosophy, the mind is seen as a tool that can be used to connect with the divine or be a barrier to that connection. By learning to control the mind and harness its power, individuals can deepen their spiritual practice and connect more fully with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Damanraj: Calm and just ruler, embodying inner strength and control, shielding loved ones from outer turmoil. symbolically, Daman signifies tranquility, and Raj represents leadership or rule. The name Damanraj evokes a sense of peacefully governing one's inner and outer world.

vedic_reference.note: Daman is a Sanskrit word meaning fearless and Damanraj is a name derived from this word, signifying a fearless ruler.

historical_references.reference: King Daman, who ruled over the region of Malwa in central India during the late 12th and early 13th centuries, is said to have been a powerful and just ruler. He is remembered for his efforts to maintain peace and stability in his kingdom, as well as his patronage of art and culture.

Daman Rao, a Maratha king who ruled over the kingdom of Jhansi in central India during the early 18th century, is known for leading a successful rebellion against the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. He is also remembered for his military prowess and his efforts to expand and strengthen his kingdom.
